g.text: In a 100-year flood, about 103,000 residents would have no shelter place on foot

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #5b6577

g.text: Residents of each flood zone by shelter outcome, today's homes and candidate shelters

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5b6577

g.text: With buses taking people up to 10 km, about 2,000 (10-year), 4,200 (100-year) and 5,300 (500-year) are left without a place.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5b6577

g.text: Shelters are candidates (schools, sports halls, civic buildings dry in that zone), not official; 1.5 km walk, 4 m² per person.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5b6577

g.text: Source: EFAS flood hazard maps (JRC), GHS-OBAT, GHS-POP 2020 (challenge data); OpenStreetMap. Team analysis. Zones are modelled with no dikes or

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5b6577

g.text: flood walls, so towns behind them (Liège, Venlo) are an upper bound. Residents are an order of magnitude.
